example_sentences.de: Unsere Nachbarn sind freundlich und hilfsbereit.
example_sentences.en: Our neighbours are friendly and helpful.

cloze.en: The bus driver greeted me in a friendly way.

words.notes: 'freundlich' = warm and polite towards others; 'nett' is the more casual everyday word.
words.germany_context: In restaurants a Trinkgeld of about 5-10% is normal when the service was friendly. You say the rounded total as you pay ('Macht 20, bitte'), you don't leave coins on the table.

example_sentences.de: Das ist sehr nett von dir!

cloze.en: He is a nice colleague.

words.notes: 'Das ist nett von dir' is the standard way to say 'that's kind of you'.
words.mnemonic: NETT sounds like 'neat' — a neat, nice person.

example_sentences.de: Sei bitte höflich zu den Nachbarn.
example_sentences.en: Please be polite to the neighbours.

cloze.de: Im Amt sollte man immer ___ bleiben.
cloze.en: At the public office you should always stay polite.

words.notes: The polite form of address is 'Sie'; using 'du' with a stranger can sound rude.
words.mnemonic: HÖFlich comes from 'Hof' (court) — behaving like at the royal court.
words.germany_context: Use 'Sie' with strangers, officials, neighbours you don't know and older people until they offer you the 'du'. Colleagues at tech companies often switch to 'du' on day one — wait for the offer.

example_sentences.de: Es ist unhöflich, zu spät zu kommen.
example_sentences.en: It is rude to arrive late.

example_sentences.de: Sein Ton am Telefon war ziemlich unhöflich.
example_sentences.en: His tone on the phone was quite rude.

cloze.en: Please don't answer so rudely!

words.notes: Prefix 'un-' turns the adjective into its opposite: höflich → unhöflich, freundlich → unfreundlich.

example_sentences.de: Sei ehrlich: Schmeckt dir das Essen?
example_sentences.en: Be honest: do you like the food?

example_sentences.de: Sie ist immer ehrlich zu mir.
example_sentences.en: She is always honest with me.

cloze.de: Ich sage dir ganz ___ meine Meinung.
cloze.en: I'll tell you my opinion quite honestly.

words.notes: 'Ehrlich gesagt …' = 'to be honest …' — an extremely common opener.

example_sentences.de: Mein Sohn ist sehr fleißig in der Schule.
example_sentences.en: My son is very hardworking at school.

example_sentences.de: Du hast diese Woche fleißig gelernt.

cloze.en: She is a hardworking student.

words.notes: A standard compliment in school reports and job references.

example_sentences.de: Am Sonntag bin ich immer faul.
Sei nicht so faul, steh bitte auf!
example_sentences.en: Don't be so lazy, please get up!

cloze.de: Mein Bruder ist zu ___ zum Aufräumen.
cloze.en: My brother is too lazy to tidy up.

words.notes: 'faul' also means 'rotten' for food: ein fauler Apfel = a rotten apple.

cloze.en: It would be clever to set off a bit earlier.

words.notes: 'klug' = wise and sensible, 'intelligent' is about brainpower, 'schlau' is the colloquial twin.
words.mnemonic: Umlaut in the comparison: klug → klüger → am klügsten.

cloze.en: She asked an intelligent question.

words.notes: Pronounced with a hard g: in-te-li-GENT, stress on the last syllable.

example_sentences.de: Entschuldigung, das war dumm von mir.
example_sentences.en: Sorry, that was stupid of me.

cloze.de: Frag ruhig, das ist keine ___ Frage.
cloze.en: Go ahead and ask, that's not a stupid question.

words.notes: Calling a person 'dumm' is an insult. For situations say 'Das ist dumm gelaufen' = that went badly.
words.mnemonic: Umlaut in the comparison: dumm → dümmer → am dümmsten.

cloze.en: Yesterday was a funny evening.

words.notes: 'lustig' = amusing. Careful with 'komisch': it means funny AND strange, often negative.

example_sentences.de: Warum bist du heute so ernst?
example_sentences.en: Why are you so serious today?

cloze.en: Are you serious about that?

words.notes: 'Im Ernst?' = 'Seriously?' and 'Das meine ich ernst' = 'I mean it'.

example_sentences.de: Unsere Straße ist abends sehr ruhig.
example_sentences.en: Our street is very quiet in the evening.

cloze.en: I'm looking for a quiet flat.

words.notes: As a particle it softens a request: 'Frag ruhig!' = 'Feel free to ask.'
words.germany_context: Ruhezeiten: quiet hours are normally 22:00-06:00, all day Sunday and in many buildings 13:00-15:00. No drilling, loud music, vacuuming or washing machine then — neighbours do complain.

example_sentences.de: Vor dem Termin bin ich immer nervös.
example_sentences.en: Before the appointment I'm always nervous.

example_sentences.de: Sei nicht nervös, du schaffst das.

cloze.en: He is waiting nervously for the result.

words.notes: Stress on the last syllable: ner-VÖS.

example_sentences.de: Als Kind war ich sehr schüchtern.
example_sentences.en: As a child I was very shy.

example_sentences.de: Sie ist schüchtern, aber sehr nett.
example_sentences.en: She is shy but very nice.

cloze.en: The new colleague seems a bit shy.

example_sentences.de: Der Supermarkt ist bis 22 Uhr offen.
example_sentences.en: The supermarket is open until 10 pm.

example_sentences.de: Er ist ein offener Mensch und redet mit jedem.
example_sentences.en: He is an open person and talks to everyone.

cloze.en: The window is still open.

words.notes: Two uses: shops/doors being open, and a person being open and frank.
words.germany_context: Almost all shops and supermarkets are closed on Sundays (Ladenschlussgesetz). Only bakeries, petrol stations, pharmacies on duty and shops inside big train stations stay open — plan your Saturday shopping.

cloze.en: My parents were quite strict.

words.notes: 'streng verboten' = strictly forbidden — you see it on many German signs.

example_sentences.de: Der Arzt war sehr geduldig mit mir.
example_sentences.en: The doctor was very patient with me.

example_sentences.de: Sei geduldig, der Bus kommt gleich.
example_sentences.en: Be patient, the bus is coming soon.

cloze.en: At the public office you have to wait patiently.

words.notes: From 'die Geduld' (patience). 'Ich habe keine Geduld' = I have no patience.

example_sentences.de: Danke, das ist sehr großzügig von dir.
example_sentences.en: Thank you, that's very generous of you.

example_sentences.de: Er gibt im Restaurant großzügig Trinkgeld.
example_sentences.en: He tips generously in the restaurant.

cloze.en: The flat has a spacious balcony.

words.notes: For rooms and flats it means 'spacious': 'ein großzügiges Wohnzimmer'.

example_sentences.de: Sei nicht so geizig, gib ihm Trinkgeld.
example_sentences.en: Don't be so stingy, give him a tip.

cloze.de: Er ist zu ___, um ein Taxi zu nehmen.
cloze.en: He is too stingy to take a taxi.

words.notes: 'Geiz ist geil' was a famous German ad slogan — 'being stingy is cool'.

example_sentences.de: Sie ist eine sehr zuverlässige Kollegin.
example_sentences.en: She is a very reliable colleague.

example_sentences.de: Mein altes Auto ist immer noch zuverlässig.
example_sentences.en: My old car is still reliable.

cloze.en: We are looking for a reliable babysitter.

words.notes: Top praise in a German Arbeitszeugnis (job reference).
words.germany_context: 'Zuverlässig' is the highest everyday compliment at a German workplace: doing exactly what you promised, by the agreed date, counts for more than being fast or loud.

example_sentences.en: The train was on time today.

cloze.en: Please be on time for the appointment.

words.notes: 'pünktlich um 8' = at 8 sharp.
words.germany_context: Termin culture: for an appointment at an Amt, doctor or viewing, arrive 5-10 minutes early. Turn up late and the slot can simply be given away — and a new Termin may be weeks later.

example_sentences.de: Dein Zimmer ist heute sehr ordentlich.
example_sentences.en: Your room is very tidy today.

cloze.en: Please keep the kitchen tidy.

words.notes: From 'die Ordnung' (order). 'Alles in Ordnung?' = 'Everything okay?'
words.germany_context: The Hausordnung of your building expects tidy stairwells and correct Mülltrennung: Papier, Gelber Sack (plastic/metal), Bio, Glas and Restmüll go in separate bins — neighbours notice mistakes.

example_sentences.de: Heute war es im Büro sehr chaotisch.
example_sentences.en: Today it was very chaotic in the office.

cloze.en: The first day at work was pretty chaotic.

words.notes: A messy person is 'ein Chaot' — said half jokingly.

cloze.de: Die Kollegen im Büro sind alle sehr ___.
cloze.en: The colleagues in the office are all very helpful.

words.notes: Literally 'ready to help' (Hilfe + bereit). Used for people, not things — for things use 'nützlich'.
words.germany_context: The Hausmeister (building caretaker) is your first contact for heating, bins, keys and small repairs — ask him before writing to the landlord.

example_sentences.de: Dein neuer Kollege ist sehr sympathisch.
example_sentences.en: Your new colleague is very likeable.

example_sentences.de: Sie war mir vom ersten Moment an sympathisch.
example_sentences.en: I liked her from the very first moment.

cloze.en: The landlord seems likeable.

words.notes: False friend: NOT 'sympathetic'. It means likeable. 'Sympathetic' = mitfühlend.

example_sentences.de: Ich bin neugierig auf das Ergebnis.

cloze.en: Don't be so nosy!

words.notes: 'neugierig auf' + accusative. Literally 'greedy for the new'.
words.mnemonic: NEU (new) + GIERIG (greedy) = greedy for news → curious.

example_sentences.de: Die Kinder sind müde und gehen ins Bett.
example_sentences.en: The children are tired and are going to bed.

cloze.de: Nach der Arbeit bin ich immer ___.
cloze.en: After work I'm always tired.

example_sentences.de: Ich bin schon seit sechs Uhr wach.
example_sentences.en: I've been awake since six o'clock.

cloze.en: The coffee makes me awake.

words.notes: Related verb: 'aufwachen' = to wake up.

example_sentences.de: Ich bin hungrig, gehen wir essen?
example_sentences.en: I'm hungry, shall we go and eat?

example_sentences.de: Die Kinder kommen hungrig aus der Schule.
example_sentences.en: The children come home from school hungry.

cloze.en: Are you this hungry already too?

words.notes: Germans say 'Ich habe Hunger' at least as often as 'Ich bin hungrig'.

example_sentences.de: Nach dem Sport bin ich immer durstig.
Das Kind ist durstig und möchte Wasser.
example_sentences.en: The child is thirsty and wants water.

cloze.de: Ich bin ___ — hast du etwas zu trinken?
cloze.en: I'm thirsty - do you have something to drink?

words.notes: More common in speech: 'Ich habe Durst'.
words.germany_context: German restaurants almost never bring free tap water. You order and pay for 'ein Wasser' — 'mit Kohlensäure' (sparkling) or 'ohne Kohlensäure' / 'still'.

cloze.en: No thanks, I'm already full.

words.notes: The polite way to decline a second helping: 'Danke, ich bin satt.'

cloze.en: The coffee tastes really good.

words.notes: Say 'Lecker!' while eating as a compliment. Waiters ask 'Hat es geschmeckt?' at the end.

example_sentences.de: Der Tee ist mir zu süß.
example_sentences.en: The tea is too sweet for me.

cloze.en: I don't like sweet drinks.

words.notes: 'süß' also means 'cute' for babies, animals and people.

cloze.en: Sea water is salty.

example_sentences.de: Mein Chef ist sauer auf mich.
example_sentences.en: My boss is annoyed with me.

cloze.en: The apple tastes sour.

words.notes: 'sauer sein auf jemanden' = to be annoyed with somebody — used constantly in spoken German.

example_sentences.de: Der Kaffee ist mir zu bitter.
example_sentences.en: The coffee is too bitter for me.

cloze.en: This medicine is very bitter.

example_sentences.de: Das Curry ist mir zu scharf.
example_sentences.en: The curry is too spicy for me.

cloze.en: I like spicy food.

words.notes: Same word for spicy food and sharp knives. Umlaut in the comparison: schärfer.
words.germany_context: At a Döner or Imbiss you will be asked 'Mit scharf?' — that means chilli sauce. Answer 'ja, bitte' or 'nein, ohne scharf'. Traditional German food is almost never spicy.

example_sentences.en: The bread rolls are completely fresh.

example_sentences.de: Ich kaufe frisches Gemüse auf dem Markt.
example_sentences.en: I buy fresh vegetables at the market.

cloze.de: Auf dem Wochenmarkt gibt es ___ Fisch.
cloze.en: At the weekly market there is fresh fish.

words.notes: Also used for weather: 'Heute ist es frisch' = it's chilly today.
words.germany_context: Bakeries are the one kind of shop allowed to open on Sunday mornings — that is where Germans get fresh Brötchen for Sunday breakfast.

example_sentences.de: Die Bananen sind noch nicht reif.

cloze.en: Is the avocado ripe yet?

words.notes: For people it means 'mature': 'Er ist sehr reif für sein Alter.'

example_sentences.de: Iss das Fleisch bitte nicht roh!
example_sentences.en: Please don't eat the meat raw!

cloze.en: The egg is still raw.

words.germany_context: Germans really do eat raw pork: 'Mett' — seasoned raw minced pork on a Brötchen with onions — is a classic party and butcher-counter snack.

example_sentences.de: Ich möchte ein gekochtes Ei zum Frühstück.
example_sentences.en: I'd like a boiled egg for breakfast.

cloze.de: Möchtest du die Eier ___ oder gebraten?
cloze.en: Would you like the eggs boiled or fried?

words.notes: Past participle of 'kochen' used as an adjective — it is not compared.

example_sentences.de: Ich nehme gebratenen Fisch mit Kartoffeln.
example_sentences.en: I'll have fried fish with potatoes.

example_sentences.de: Das Hähnchen ist gebraten, nicht gekocht.
example_sentences.en: The chicken is roasted, not boiled.

cloze.en: There are fried vegetables on the plate.

words.notes: Past participle of the irregular verb 'braten' (er brät).

example_sentences.en: Do you have a vegetarian dish?

cloze.en: This pizza is vegetarian.

words.notes: 'vegan' = no animal products at all; menus often mark dishes with (v) or (vg).
words.germany_context: Germany is very easy for vegetarians: every supermarket has a big veggie section, and menus mark dishes 'vegetarisch' or 'vegan'. In a restaurant just ask 'Was haben Sie Vegetarisches?'

example_sentences.de: Heute ist es sonnig und warm.

example_sentences.en: We're looking for a sunny flat.

cloze.en: At the weekend it will be sunny.

example_sentences.de: Im November ist es oft regnerisch.

cloze.en: It's going to be a rainy weekend.

example_sentences.de: An der Nordsee ist es fast immer windig.
example_sentences.en: At the North Sea it's almost always windy.

cloze.de: Nimm eine Jacke mit, es ist ___.
cloze.en: Take a jacket, it's windy.

example_sentences.en: In the morning it was foggy.

example_sentences.de: Im Herbst ist es hier oft neblig.
example_sentences.en: In autumn it's often foggy here.

cloze.en: Outside it's cold and foggy.

words.notes: Also written 'nebelig'. From 'der Nebel' (fog).

example_sentences.de: Im Sommer ist es hier oft schwül.
example_sentences.en: In summer it's often muggy here.

example_sentences.de: Heute ist es schwül, es gibt bestimmt ein Gewitter.
example_sentences.en: Today it's muggy, there's sure to be a thunderstorm.

cloze.en: The air is muggy and heavy.

words.notes: Careful: 'schwül' = muggy, 'schwul' = gay. One umlaut changes everything.

example_sentences.de: Im Bad ist die Luft sehr feucht.
example_sentences.en: The air in the bathroom is very humid.

cloze.en: The wall in the bedroom is damp.

words.germany_context: Damp walls mean Schimmel (mould), and in a rented flat that quickly becomes a dispute with the landlord. Germans 'stoßlüften': open the windows wide for 5-10 minutes several times a day instead of tilting them.

cloze.en: Please put on the dry socks.

words.notes: On wine labels: trocken (dry), halbtrocken, lieblich (sweet).

example_sentences.de: Es regnet, ich werde gleich nass.
example_sentences.en: It's raining, I'll get wet in a moment.

cloze.en: Careful, the floor is wet.

example_sentences.de: Der Boden ist frisch geputzt und glatt.
example_sentences.en: The floor is freshly cleaned and slippery.

cloze.de: Im Winter sind die Wege oft ___.
cloze.en: In winter the paths are often slippery.

words.notes: Weather warning word: 'Glatteis' = black ice.
words.germany_context: Räum- und Streupflicht: in winter tenants or owners must clear snow and grit the pavement in front of the house, usually from 07:00 (Sundays 09:00) until 20:00. If someone slips, you can be liable.

example_sentences.de: Zieh bequeme Schuhe an, wir laufen viel.
example_sentences.en: Put on comfortable shoes, we'll walk a lot.

cloze.en: The sofa is old but comfortable.

words.notes: For a person 'bequem' means comfort-loving, almost lazy.

cloze.en: This café here is really cosy.

words.notes: Hard to translate: cosy plus relaxed and unhurried. 'Machen wir es uns gemütlich' = let's get comfy.
words.germany_context: 'Gemütlichkeit' is a core German idea — warm light, candles, no rush. Telling someone their home or their Kneipe is 'gemütlich' is a real compliment.

cloze.en: We live in a modern house.

words.notes: Stress on the second syllable: mo-DERN.
words.germany_context: In flat ads 'Neubau' means a modern building (good insulation, often a lift), 'Altbau' means an old one with high ceilings, more charm and usually higher heating costs.

cloze.en: The word sounds a bit old-fashioned.

example_sentences.de: Ein Fahrrad ist in der Stadt praktisch.
example_sentences.en: A bike is practical in the city.

cloze.en: Your new app is really practical.

words.notes: As an adverb it also means 'practically/almost': 'Es ist praktisch fertig.'

example_sentences.de: Danke, dein Tipp war sehr nützlich.
example_sentences.en: Thanks, your tip was very useful.

example_sentences.de: Das ist eine nützliche App für den Alltag.
example_sentences.en: That's a useful app for everyday life.

cloze.en: Learning German is very useful.

words.notes: From 'der Nutzen' (benefit). For people who like helping use 'hilfsbereit'.

cloze.en: Careful, the dog is dangerous!

example_sentences.de: Die Gegend ist auch nachts sicher.
example_sentences.en: The area is safe at night too.

cloze.de: Ich bin mir nicht ___, ob er kommt.
cloze.en: I'm not sure whether he's coming.

words.notes: Two meanings: 'safe' and 'sure'. As an adverb it means 'surely/certainly': 'Er kommt sicher.'

cloze.en: The traffic was totally crazy today.

words.notes: 'verrückt nach etwas sein' = to be crazy about something.

example_sentences.de: Er hat sich gestern seltsam verhalten.

cloze.en: The smell in the hallway is strange.

words.notes: Synonyms: 'komisch' (more spoken) and 'merkwürdig' (a bit more formal).

example_sentences.en: Today was a normal working day.

cloze.en: Is this price normal here?

words.notes: 'ganz normal' is used constantly to reassure someone.

cloze.en: Bratwurst is a typical dish here.

words.notes: 'Typisch!' on its own means 'Typical!' — mildly annoyed.

example_sentences.de: Fußball ist in Deutschland sehr beliebt.
example_sentences.en: Football is very popular in Germany.

cloze.en: The park is popular with families.

words.notes: 'beliebt bei' + dative = popular with somebody.

example_sentences.de: Diese Straße ist für ihre Cafés bekannt.
example_sentences.en: This street is known for its cafés.
Does that seem familiar to you?

cloze.en: His name is not familiar to me.

words.notes: 'ein Bekannter / eine Bekannte' as a noun = an acquaintance, less close than a Freund.

example_sentences.de: Köln ist für seinen Dom berühmt.
example_sentences.en: Cologne is famous for its cathedral.

cloze.en: This museum is famous worldwide.

words.notes: 'berühmt für' + accusative = famous for something.

example_sentences.de: Der Aufzug ist schon wieder kaputt.

cloze.de: Das Fahrrad ist ___, ich muss laufen.
cloze.en: The bike is broken, I have to walk.

words.notes: Also colloquial for 'exhausted': 'Ich bin total kaputt.'
words.germany_context: If something breaks in a rented flat, report it to the Vermieter or Hausverwaltung in writing straight away — repairs are usually their job, and damage you never reported can be taken from your Kaution.

cloze.en: German grammar is complicated but logical.

words.germany_context: German admin is paper-heavy: book a Termin online, then bring your passport, Meldebescheinigung and every document on the list. One missing paper usually means a completely new appointment.

cloze.en: The long journey was quite exhausting.

words.notes: From 'sich anstrengen' = to make an effort.

example_sentences.de: Ich bin mit meiner Arbeit zufrieden.
Der Chef war zufrieden mit dem Ergebnis.
example_sentences.en: The boss was satisfied with the result.

cloze.en: Are you satisfied with the flat?

words.notes: Always with 'mit' + dative: zufrieden mit dem Preis.

example_sentences.de: Sie ist stolz auf ihre Kinder.
example_sentences.en: She is proud of her children.

cloze.de: Er ist ___ auf sein neues Auto.
cloze.en: He is proud of his new car.

words.notes: 'stolz auf' + accusative.

example_sentences.de: Vor dem Flug war sie sehr aufgeregt.
example_sentences.en: Before the flight she was very excited.

cloze.de: Die Kinder sind vor Weihnachten total ___.
cloze.en: The children are totally excited before Christmas.

words.notes: Covers both happy excitement and jittery nerves.

example_sentences.de: Ich bin von dem Film enttäuscht.
Er war enttäuscht über die Absage.
example_sentences.en: He was disappointed about the rejection.

cloze.en: She looked very disappointed yesterday.

words.notes: 'enttäuscht von' + dative (a person or thing), 'enttäuscht über' + accusative (an event).

example_sentences.de: Sie war überrascht, mich hier zu sehen.
example_sentences.en: She was surprised to see me here.

cloze.en: Why are you so surprised?

words.notes: Verb: 'überraschen'. Noun: 'die Überraschung'.

example_sentences.de: Sei nicht eifersüchtig auf deinen Bruder.
example_sentences.en: Don't be jealous of your brother.

cloze.de: Der Hund ist ___ auf das Baby.
cloze.en: The dog is jealous of the baby.

words.notes: 'eifersüchtig auf' + accusative. For envying someone's things use 'neidisch'.

example_sentences.de: Sie ist in ihren Kollegen verliebt.
example_sentences.en: She is in love with her colleague.
The two of them are newly in love.

cloze.en: I think he is in love.

words.notes: 'verliebt in' + accusative: verliebt in ihn.

example_sentences.de: Ich bin von dem Lärm total genervt.
example_sentences.en: I'm totally annoyed by the noise.
She sounded annoyed on the phone.

cloze.de: Nach zwei Stunden Warten war er ___.
cloze.en: After two hours of waiting he was annoyed.

words.notes: Everyday spoken German: 'Das nervt!' = 'That's annoying!'

cloze.en: Are you married or single?

words.notes: Official form word. In conversation people usually say 'Ich bin Single'.
words.germany_context: 'Familienstand' (marital status) is asked on nearly every German form — Anmeldung, tax, insurance. The four options are ledig, verheiratet, geschieden, verwitwet.

example_sentences.de: Wir sind seit fünf Jahren verheiratet.
example_sentences.en: We've been married for five years.

cloze.en: He is married to a doctor.

words.notes: 'verheiratet mit' + dative.
words.germany_context: Marriage changes your Steuerklasse: couples can pick III/V or IV/IV, which often means noticeably more net pay. Marriages are registered at the Standesamt, and only the civil ceremony is legally binding.

example_sentences.de: Sie ist seit zwei Jahren geschieden.
example_sentences.en: She has been divorced for two years.

cloze.de: Er ist ___ und hat zwei Kinder.
cloze.en: He is divorced and has two children.

words.notes: Past participle of 'scheiden'. The noun is 'die Scheidung' (divorce).

example_sentences.de: Sie ist im vierten Monat schwanger.

cloze.en: Congratulations, you're pregnant!

words.notes: Only used for the woman: 'Wir bekommen ein Kind' is how a couple says it.
words.germany_context: Pregnant employees are protected by Mutterschutz (6 weeks before and 8 weeks after the birth) and parents can claim Elterngeld and Elternzeit. Tell your employer early — the protection only starts once they know.

example_sentences.de: Der Parkplatz ist für behinderte Menschen.
example_sentences.en: The parking space is for disabled people.

example_sentences.de: Ist das Gebäude für behinderte Personen zugänglich?
example_sentences.en: Is the building accessible for disabled people?

cloze.en: This seat is for disabled passengers.

words.notes: Careful: as an insult 'behindert' is offensive slang. The respectful terms are 'Menschen mit Behinderung' or 'beeinträchtigt'.
words.germany_context: With a Schwerbehindertenausweis (official disability card) you get reduced or free public transport, tax relief, extra holiday days and stronger protection against dismissal.

example_sentences.de: Die Frau mit den blonden Haaren ist meine Chefin.
example_sentences.en: The woman with the blond hair is my boss.

cloze.en: He has short blond hair.

words.notes: Hair colours: blond, braun, schwarz, rot, grau.

example_sentences.de: Der dunkelhaarige Junge ist mein Sohn.
example_sentences.en: The dark-haired boy is my son.

cloze.en: Both children are dark-haired.

words.notes: Built like a compound: dunkel + Haar + -ig. Same pattern: rothaarig, langhaarig.

example_sentences.de: Sie ist in letzter Zeit sehr schlank geworden.
example_sentences.en: She has become very slim recently.

cloze.en: My sister is slim and athletic.

words.notes: 'schlank' is the polite word; 'dünn' can sound like a criticism.

cloze.de: Für diesen Job muss man ___ sein.
cloze.en: For this job you have to be athletic.

words.notes: From 'der Sport'. Also used for clothes and cars.
words.germany_context: Sport in Germany mostly happens in a 'Verein' (club). A yearly membership is often cheaper than a gym and is one of the easiest ways to meet Germans.

cloze.de: Sie wohnt in einem ___ kleinen Dorf.
cloze.en: She lives in a pretty little village.

words.notes: 'hübsch' is lighter than 'schön' and works for people, clothes and places.
